decisive_items: brain MRI showed chronic periventricular white matter changes
A diagnostic algorithm for dizziness suggested a low probability of central or peripheral vestibular origin
Repeat brain MRI showed no signs of recent vascular lesions
response.rationale: Chronic periventricular white matter changes are the most objective and persisting finding, consistent with small vessel disease and progressive unsteadiness; carotid stenosis was overestimated and vestibular/vascular causes were otherwise excluded.

rejected.why: Carotid stenosis was overestimated due to tortuosity and TCD showed normal hemodynamics, so atherosclerotic disease is not the likely cause of the recurrent dizziness.

Though vertigo could suggest vertebrobasilar insufficiency, HINTS was negative, the diagnostic algorithm indicated low vestibular probability, and repeat MRI/TCD showed no acute or hemodynamic posterior-circulation abnormality.
